questions.q: Suppose $A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$ is a real matrix with non-zero entries, $ad - bc = 0$ and $A^{2} = A$. Then, $a + d$ equals
questions.solution:
We have,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$A^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$A^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}a^{2} + bc & ab + bd \\ ac + cd & bc + d^{2}\end{cases}\right]$

Given, $A^{2} = A$ and $ad - bc = 0$

$∴ \left[\begin{cases}a^{2} + bc & ab + bd \\ ac + cd & bc + d^{2}\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}a & b \\ c & d\end{cases}\right]$

$ab + bd = b$

$b\left(a + d\right) = b$

$⇒ a + d = 1$

Let $A = \left({a}_{ij}\right)^{1} \le i, \mathop{j}_{¯}3$ be a $3 \times 3$ invertible matrix where each ${a}_{ii}$ is a real number. Denote the inverse of the matrix $A$ by $A^{- 1}.$ If $\mathop{∑}_{itl}^{3}{a}_{ij} = 1$
for $1 \le i \le 3,$ then
options: sum of the diagonal entries of $A$ is $1$
sum of each row of $A^{- 1}$ is $1$
sum of each row and each column of $A^{- 1}$ is $1$
sum of the diagonal entries of $A^{- 1}$ is $1$
questions.solution:
Sum of elements in each row of $A$ is $1.$

So, $A\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$
$⇒ A^{- 1}A\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = A^{- 1}\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$
$⇒ \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = A^{- 1}\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$
$⇒$ sum of elements in each row of $A^{- 1}$ is $1$
